events_chronological: A career field officer sells two missiles in a Middle Eastern capital and loses track of one, which an arms dealer carries off.
In an oil-rich desert state the drilling rights held by a large western company are handed instead to a Chinese firm.
A migrant labourer on the state's oilfield is laid off along with his father when the contract changes hands.
The western company announces a merger with a small firm that has just won drilling rights in central Asia.
A government inquiry opens into the merger, and a young lawyer is instructed to turn up exactly enough corruption to satisfy it.
An energy analyst brings his family to a party at the ruler's palace, where his small son is electrocuted in the swimming pool.
The ruler's elder son takes on the analyst as an adviser, out of guilt and out of conviction both.
The labourer and his father queue for work and are drawn into a school where a preacher takes a close interest in them.
The field officer is sent to arrange the killing of the elder son, who is judged unfriendly to western interests.
He is betrayed to a militia, tortured and dumped, and comes home to find his own service suspects him.
The elder son sets out his programme: the rights go to the highest bidder, the parliament gets real power, and women get the vote.
The lawyer establishes that an executive at the small firm paid bribes for the central Asian field, and delivers him to the inquiry along with his own mentor.
The ruler names his younger son rather than his elder as successor.
The field officer works out that the killing is going ahead regardless and drives into the desert to warn the prince.
The labourer and another young man take the missing missile out to sea in a fishing boat.
A missile from a drone destroys the prince's convoy in the desert, killing him, his family, the analyst's employer and the field officer.
The labourer steers the boat into the side of a new tanker and the missile detonates.
The merger goes through, and the men who engineered the whole of it are photographed collecting a prize.
nonlinear_category_reason: Every strand keeps its own forward order and nothing is ever shown out of turn in time; the inversions are only between strands running at the same moment, which the telling cuts between sideways. Four strands on three continents advance together towards a single week, cut between without captions.
syuzhet_notes: Four strands are cut into one another from the opening with almost no captions, and none of them is a flashback: they are happening at once in different countries and converge on the same fortnight.
fabula_notes: The ordering follows the causal chain from the lost missile and the transferred drilling rights. Concurrent strands can be ranked either way.

events.content: A covert sale places two weapons in a capital; one leaves the transaction in an unauthorised dealer's hands and disappears from official sight.
events.location: a warehouse in a desert capital

reader: one portable missile has escaped the controlled sale

questions.q72_1: where will the missile that escaped the sale reappear?

events.content: A state awards its main field to a new foreign bidder, abruptly displacing the western company that had treated access as permanent.

reader: the transfer of drilling rights threatens a powerful company

questions.q72_2: how will the displaced company replace the lost oil field?

events.content: The contract change reaches the labour camp as unemployment, leaving a young worker and his father in a queue with no income or status.

migrant labourer: the oilfield no longer has work for him
reader: corporate displacement has produced personal precarity

questions.q72_3: where can the dismissed labourer find work and belonging?

events.content: To replace the lost field, the corporation seeks a smaller firm whose distant drilling concession promises comparable access.

reader: the proposed merger is the company's route back to reserves

events.content: Regulators open a review, while the lawyer is privately told to uncover enough misconduct to legitimise a result already desired.

lawyer: the inquiry wants controlled sacrifice rather than full truth
reader: the merger investigation has a predetermined limit

questions.q72_4: whose corruption will the controlled inquiry sacrifice?

events.content: At a royal reception, an unsafe underwater light turns a family outing into a sudden death that binds the analyst to the ruling household.

energy analyst: his child has died on palace grounds
reader: private grief will connect the analyst to the elder prince

questions.q72_5: what relationship will grow out of the child's death at the palace?

events.content: Guilt opens the meeting, but the prince's reform programme gives the bereaved analyst a reason to remain as adviser.

energy analyst: the prince intends to reform the oil economy
reader: grief and political conviction have joined the analyst to the prince

events.content: Food, lessons and sustained attention at a religious school answer needs the labour camp no longer meets, drawing the unemployed pair inward.

migrant labourer: the school offers belonging and a cause
reader: economic exclusion has made the labourer vulnerable to recruitment

events.content: The field officer is handed a deniable operation against the reforming heir, framed as routine protection of strategic interests.

field officer: his service wants the elder prince removed
reader: the reform programme has triggered a covert death order

questions.q72_6: will the order to kill the elder prince ultimately be carried out?

events.content: The operation is betrayed before execution; captivity and repudiation teach the officer that his own service is prepared to erase him.

field officer: the mission was compromised and his service suspects him
reader: the officer has become expendable to the system he served

events.content: He proposes open bidding, representative government and votes for women, converting business rivalry into an explicit threat to entrenched power.

reader: the elder prince's agenda challenges both family succession and foreign interests

questions.q72_7: can the reform programme survive the interests arrayed against it?

events.content: Following the bribe trail gives the inquiry an executive and the lawyer's own mentor, containing the scandal without threatening the merger's architects.

lawyer: his advancement depends on sacrificing his mentor
reader: the inquiry has isolated acceptable blame

events.content: The succession bypasses the reformer, making family authority another instrument that protects the existing oil arrangement.

elder prince: his father has denied him succession
reader: institutional power has closed around the reformer

events.content: Having recognised that the assassination survived his failed mission, the disavowed officer races towards the convoy he was once ordered to destroy.

field officer: a remote strike is still imminent
reader: the former assassin is now trying to prevent the killing

questions.q72_8: can the field officer reach the convoy before the strike?

events.content: The missing shoulder weapon reappears with the two recruits as they take a small craft towards the newly opened tanker route.

reader: the lost missile and the dismissed worker have entered the same attack plan

events.content: A remote missile reaches the desert before the officer's warning can, killing the reformer, his family, the analyst's employer and would-be rescuer together.

reader: the reform programme and the attempt to save it have been eliminated

events.content: The fishing boat strikes the tanker and converts a weapon misplaced at the beginning into the labourer's final act.

reader: the missile's untracked path ends in a successful suicide attack

events.content: With the inquiry contained and rivals dead, the transaction closes and its senior beneficiaries pose for a photograph of respectable success.

reader: the institutions that generated the violence emerge rewarded
